A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZO Fine-tuner and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D. Retained material can be matched despite substantial layout changes and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments across four LLMs and seven datasets, derivative-checkpoint transfer, ablations, and runtime and memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds mathematical-reasoning evaluations, meta-training and trajectory ablations, first-order accuracy comparisons, and accuracy curves.

M1.justification: The per-block PertNN architecture, meta-objective, normalization, periodic resets, and gradient-stopping approximation are retained. Revised sampling equations align the main text with the multiplicative perturbation construction already documented in v1 Appendix B.3; they do not establish a different implemented optimizer.

E1.justification: v2 adds a distinct mathematical-reasoning setting: Qwen2.5-14B is fine-tuned on MetaMathQA and evaluated on GSM8K and MATH-500. This extends coverage to longer-solution reasoning tasks beyond the retained seven-task NLP suite.

E2.justification: New Tables 11–12 include first-order Adam in predictive-performance comparisons; v1 included first-order methods only in memory comparisons. Table 5 also supplies an untuned base-model reference. The original main-table comparator lineup remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Added protocols include 10,000-step MetaMathQA fine-tuning followed by separate math-benchmark testing, alternative meta-training sources, and SGD-versus-Adam trajectory controls with loss summarized over 4,000-step intervals. Existing main-experiment learning-rate grids, batch sizes, and step budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through meta-training-dataset ablations (Table 6), SGD-versus-Adam trajectory ablations (Tables 13–14), and test accuracy/F1 convergence curves (Figure 7). These supplement, rather than replace, the existing normalization, reset, sharing, learning-rate, and single-versus-multiple-dataset analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C.8 newly announces fixed-seed reproduction scripts, providing limited seed-related information. This does not establish additional runs: neither version specifies repeated-run counts or numerical seeds, and Figure 2 retains the same smoothed-loss standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: All 280 numerical entries in Table 1 are unchanged. Substantial new results include GSM8K accuracy of 85.6 versus MeZO's 81.4 and MATH-500 accuracy of 54.6 versus 53.0, plus meta-training ablations, trajectory comparisons, first-order reference scores, and accuracy curves. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under its original settings.

T1.justification: v2 repairs a covariance inconsistency in the main mathematical description: perturbations use u = Σz with covariance ΣΣᵀ, replacing the earlier square-root construction while retaining the Frobenius-norm normalization. This makes the stated second-moment identity consistent. Appendix D's assumptions, bounds, and proof are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a compact per-block learned zeroth-order optimizer trained once per base model and reused across tasks and derivative checkpoints. The abstract and introduction retain the 82.1% loss-win and 2.5% average accuracy-improvement claims. New experiments primarily support the existing transfer claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of mathematical transfer, meta-training-source robustness, and trajectory choice. It explicitly limits evaluation to the MeZO-style regime and leaves combinations with LoRA, quantization, and offloading for future work. The new assertion of consistently beating MeZO overstates Table 6, which contains one contrary SQuAD result.

D1.justification: Appendix C.8 newly specifies, for LLaMA-3.2-1B on COPA, resets every five epochs and 15 total training epochs, alongside tuning rationale and claimed checkpoint/script releases. v2 also discloses use of MeZO prompt templates. These document existing procedures rather than demonstrate changes to them.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for MetaMath, GSM8K, and the MATH-500 evaluation source: Yu et al., Cobbe et al., and Lightman et al. The established zeroth-order and learning-to-learn positioning remains largely intact. Sun et al. appears in the expanded main related-work discussion but was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. Local rewrites affect the abstract, motivation, transfer discussion, conclusion, and limitations; acknowledgments, an impact statement, and Appendices C.6–C.8 are added. Author-affiliation and heading text also change.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference-style main paper, with extensively resized and rearranged tables and retypeset algorithms. Appendix plots move to the end. Six tables and Figure 7 are added; the original derivative-transfer and sharing tables are retained with exchanged numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central reuse claim through transfer to mathematical reasoning and controls on meta-training data and trajectory choice. First-order accuracy references and concrete reset/training disclosures improve interpretation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses: Table 6 contradicts the new uniform-superiority wording, and several added first-order-reference tables report ZO Fine-tuner scores differing from Table 1 without explaining the settings.
